inputs.notes:
OWNER-FCF DCF (US operating company, HVAC/refrigeration industrial) per SKILL.md routing table row 2 (non-US-tech operating company / cyclical industrial) -- adaptations file read but the currency, lease and NCI items do not apply (USD filer/USD quote, immaterial leases, no NCI); the cyclical risk-charged-once and working-capital-sign items DO apply and are addressed below. FIRST valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF/Drivers file, no MEMORY.md entry) -- fresh build.

HISTORICAL CAGRS ARE NOT USABLE AS A GROWTH ANCHOR. Carrier completed the ~$13.4B Viessmann Climate Solutions acquisition in Jan 2024 (funded ~80% cash/20% stock) and divested Fire & Security, Industrial Fire, Access Solutions and Commercial Refrigeration through 2024-2025, with the Riello (oil/gas burner) sale and NORESCO exit ongoing into 2026. Reported revenue/equity/EPS CAGRs FY2022-FY2025 mix a shrinking legacy portfolio, a large debt-funded acquisition, and multiple divestiture gains/losses -- none is a clean organic growth signal, so historical_growth below is reported for completeness and explicitly NOT used as growth_rates. Growth is instead anchored on FY2026 guidance (revenue ~$23B, mid-to-high-single-digit organic growth, raised from ~$22B at Q2-26 earnings) and the disclosed structural drivers (data-center cooling revenue guided to ~$2B FY2026, doubling for the second consecutive year; commercial HVAC backlog >$8B; A2L refrigerant transition; European heat-pump electrification), decelerating over the 10-year horizon toward a 4.0% terminal rate that blends secular HVAC/electrification tailwinds against structurally cyclical residential demand.

FY0 = FY2025 ($21,747M), the first full year with a complete Viessmann contribution and materially complete Fire&Security/Commercial Refrigeration divestitures, i.e. the cleanest available base-year mix. Net debt and share count are refreshed to the Q1 2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-03-31), the latest available filing, per the always-refresh-anchors rule; FY2025 10-K net debt would be six months stale.

MARGIN BUILD: FY2025 GAAP EBITDA margin (EBITDA per company/CSV convention, $3,446M/$21,747M) = 15.85%, GAAP EBIT margin 9.99%. Management's own FY2026 guidance (~$3.5B adjusted operating profit / ~$23B revenue = 15.2% ADJUSTED operating margin) implies a ~5.2pp gap to the FY2025 GAAP EBIT margin, of which ~3.8pp is non-cash Viessmann purchase-accounting intangible amortization ($884M of the $1,274M FY2025 total D&A is intangible amortization per XBRL AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets, only $383M is real depreciation) and the remainder is one-off separation/restructuring/integration cost add-backs company management excludes from 'adjusted'. This DCF uses the GAAP/component build (EBITDA -> D&A -> EBIT -> tax -> NOPAT), NOT the company's adjusted figures, so D&A is modelled explicitly and declines gradually as a % of revenue (5.86% FY2025 -> ~4.3% by year 10) as the Viessmann intangible amortization dollar amount is roughly flat-to-declining against a growing revenue base, while EBITDA margin itself ramps from 15.85% toward a mature ~17.5% (base case) as: (a) tariff cost pass-through catches up to pricing (explicitly guided as a FY2026 drag, expected to close through 2026-2027), (b) the ~$400M FY2026 productivity/cost-action target and prior $100M 2025 overhead cuts land, and (c) mix shifts toward higher-margin commercial HVAC/data-center cooling and away from lower-margin residential/new-construction.

SBC is the smallest of any ticker in this folder at 0.34% of revenue (mature industrial, not a tech-style equity-comp model) -- held roughly flat as a % of revenue rather than declining, since there is no maturity glide path to model (it is already at a mature-industrial floor).

WORKING CAPITAL: Carrier is a manufacturer/distributor (inventory + receivables typically exceed payables for an industrial OEM), so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash) rather than the positive capture used for prepaid-subscription models -- consistent with the owner-fcf.md checklist item on working-capital sign matching the balance sheet.

CASH TAX: FY2025 implied cash tax rate on EBIT was ~33.6% ($729M / $2,172M EBIT), elevated versus the US statutory-plus-state-plus-foreign blended norm (~24-26%) for a company of this profile -- FY2024's cash tax of $2,126M was a clear one-off (divestiture gains taxed at exit, against only $563M of that year's operating cash flow, i.e. tax payments tied to gain-on-sale bookings rather than run-rate operations). Base case ramps cash tax DOWN from the elevated ~33.6% FY2025 print toward a ~25% steady blended US/Europe statutory rate by year 5, as one-off divestiture-related tax payments roll off.

BUYBACKS: $2,892M FY2025 cash outflow (financing activities, confirmed via SEC XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock) funds the flat share count assumption -- Carrier is an active repurchaser (new $5B authorization announced 2026, partly funded by Riello sale proceeds), so the flat-count convention is being genuinely paid for in cash, not a modelling fiction.

RISK CHARGED ONCE: a single 8.5% WACC is used across all three scenarios (no per-scenario WACC stacking); cyclical/execution/tariff/AI-capex-dependency risk is expressed through the probability weights and the bear-case driver path, not an additional WACC premium on top of scenario weighting.

BAND_POSITION CAVEAT: house ($42.56) and street ($44.52) weighted IVs sit only ~$2 apart because Carrier's SBC is just 0.35% of revenue (a mature industrial, not an equity-comp-heavy tech model) -- the house/street band is genuinely narrow, not an error. band_position (704.6) is therefore a large, uninformative percentage for this ticker: it measures how far the CURRENT PRICE sits outside a ~$2-wide band, not a meaningful SBC-accounting-regime read. Treat house intrinsic_value/weighted_iv as the operative figures; band_position should be read as "far outside the band" rather than literally.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 management guidance (revenue ~$23B, mid-to-high-single-digit organic growth), NOT a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical revenue/equity/FCF CAGRs above are NOT usable growth anchors and are reported for completeness only. FY2022-FY2025 straddles the ~$13.4B debt-and-stock-funded Viessmann acquisition (closed Jan 2024) and the divestiture of Fire & Security, Industrial Fire, Access Solutions and Commercial Refrigeration (2024-2025), so revenue, equity and FCF all show step-changes from M&A rather than organic compounding -- e.g. equity CAGR of ~20% mixes Viessmann stock-consideration issuance, divestiture gains/losses, and buybacks, none of which describe an ongoing growth rate. Growth in assumptions.base is instead anchored on FY2026 guidance and the disclosed structural drivers (data-center doubling, commercial HVAC backlog, electrification), decelerating toward a 4.0% terminal rate; see inputs.notes for the full reasoning.

base.narrative: Guidance is met and the margin-recovery plan works roughly on management's stated timeline: tariff pricing catches up through 2026-2027, the ~$400M 2026 productivity program lands, and the mix shift toward commercial HVAC/data-center cooling (backlog >$8B, data-center revenue doubling to ~$2B in FY2026 and continuing to scale with new Texas/Alabama capacity from Q1 2027) offsets a structurally softer but not collapsing residential replacement cycle. Revenue decelerates from the guided ~5.8% FY2026 pace toward a 4.0% terminal rate reflecting durable HVAC electrification/A2L-transition and data-center secular demand blended with residential cyclicality. EBITDA margin ramps from FY2025's 15.85% to a mature 17.5% as one-off integration/restructuring costs and tariff-timing drag roll off. Cash tax normalizes from FY2025's divestiture-inflated ~33.6% toward a 25% steady blended rate.

bull.narrative: AI data-center cooling scales faster and further than guided: the ~$2B FY2026 figure keeps doubling into 2027-2028 as the Texas/Alabama capacity comes online ahead of schedule and ZutaCore liquid cooling wins meaningful hyperscaler share against Vertiv/JCI/Trane, while commercial HVAC's >$8B backlog converts at high-single-digit growth and residential demand troughs and re-accelerates as rates ease. Productivity actions and full tariff pass-through land faster than management's own timeline, pushing EBITDA margin to ~19.5% (well past the FY2026 adjusted-operating-margin guide of 15.2%) as scale and mix improve together. Capex rises further to fund additional data-center capacity, a genuine reinvestment in the highest-return growth vector, not a cost overrun.

bear.narrative: Residential destocking proves more persistent than guided, tariff costs are never fully passed through (management's own Q2-26 commentary shows pricing repeatedly lagging cost increases), and a broader AI capex slowdown removes the data-center re-rating catalyst just as Vertiv/Johnson Controls/Trane/Daikin competition intensifies in a space where Carrier's ZutaCore liquid-cooling technology is unproven at scale. Viessmann integration and the simultaneous Riello sale/NORESCO exit generate recurring one-off costs (the guided ~$0.05 FY2026 EPS drag persists rather than being a single-year item) instead of the clean cost-out management targets, holding EBITDA margin near 15.5% rather than recovering. Post-Viessmann leverage (~2.3x net debt/EBITDA) constrains the pace of buybacks/dividend growth if free cash flow disappoints, and elevated cash tax normalizes only slowly.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance is met on roughly its own timeline: mid-single-digit revenue growth decelerating to a 4% terminal rate as electrification/A2L-transition and data-center secular demand offset residential cyclicality; EBITDA margin ramps from 15.85% to a mature 17.5% as tariff pass-through completes and the $400M 2026 productivity program lands; cash tax normalizes from FY2025's divestiture-inflated 33.6% to a 25% steady rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-center cooling keeps doubling past FY2026, commercial HVAC's >$8B backlog converts at high-single-digit growth, and full tariff/productivity pass-through pushes EBITDA margin to ~19.5% -- the market's ~$78 average analyst price target scenario.
scenario_narratives.bear: Residential destocking persists, tariff costs are never fully passed through, an AI-capex slowdown removes the data-center catalyst amid intensifying Vertiv/JCI/Trane/Daikin competition, and Viessmann/divestiture integration costs recur rather than rolling off -- EBITDA margin holds near 15.5% and leverage constrains capital return.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 25% given (a) two consecutive quarters (Q1/Q2 2026) of adjusted EPS margin miss despite revenue beats -- a live execution problem, not a hypothetical risk -- and (b) genuine multi-year integration complexity from running the Viessmann integration, the Riello sale and the NORESCO exit simultaneously, each with its own disclosed one-off cost drag. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because the data-center growth story, while real and well-evidenced (order growth, backlog), still depends on a relatively narrow set of hyperscaler capex decisions and unproven-at-scale liquid-cooling technology -- the bull case needs both the data-center scale-up AND a full margin recovery to go right, not just one of them.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Carrier is a structurally repositioned industrial: post-Viessmann/post-divestiture, it is a larger, more Europe-exposed, more heat-pump/electrification-levered HVAC pure-play with a genuinely new and fast-scaling AI data-center cooling growth vector layered on top of a still-cyclical residential core. The valuation question is not whether the growth drivers are real (order growth and backlog data corroborate them) but whether management converts revenue growth into margin recovery on its own guided timeline, given two consecutive quarters of margin disappointment against tariff and mix headwinds even as revenue beat. The current price (~$56) sits well below the average sell-side target (~$78), which is either a genuine value gap on an unrecognized data-center story or a rational discount for integration/execution risk that has already shown up twice in 2026 earnings prints.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin-recovery execution: two consecutive quarters of adjusted EPS decline despite revenue beats (tariff timing, unfavorable mix, lower JV income) directly threaten the base case's EBITDA-margin ramp to 17.5%

AI data-center capex cycle dependency: the most valuable growth narrative rests on continued hyperscaler capital spending and Carrier's unproven-at-scale ZutaCore liquid-cooling technology against Vertiv/JCI/Trane/Daikin
Residential HVAC cyclicality: high-single-digit declines from channel destocking are a direct offset to commercial/data-center strength and the largest swing factor in consolidated organic growth

Post-Viessmann leverage (~2.3x net debt/EBITDA) and simultaneous multi-transaction portfolio restructuring (Riello sale, NORESCO exit) create ongoing execution and one-time-cost risk layered on top of integration risk

Tariff and trade-policy exposure given Carrier's global manufacturing/sourcing footprint, with management's own commentary showing pricing has repeatedly lagged cost increases rather than fully offsetting them
